questions.question: How do you query records with ActiveRecord?
questions.title: ActiveRecord Basic Querying
questions.direct_answer: ActiveRecord gives you chainable query methods instead of raw SQL: Model.where(active: true), Model.order(created_at: :desc), Model.limit(10), Model.first, Model.find(id), Model.all. Each returns an ActiveRecord relation you can chain (where(...).order(...).limit(...)) until you trigger it with a terminal method (first, to_a, each). This is the ActiveRecord Query Interface — composable, database-agnostic, and safe from SQL injection for the common cases.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know the chainable query methods (where/order/limit/first/find) and that they return a relation you can chain until a terminal call.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Calling .all and loading everything, or using raw SQL with interpolation where a query method is safer.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: where/order/limit/first/find are chainable and return a Relation; chain until a terminal method (first, to_a, each) runs the SQL.

sections.title: What the interviewer wants
sections.content: Define ActiveRecord Basic Querying simply, show a small example, and mention the main trade-off or edge case.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: ActiveRecord gives chainable query methods (where, order, limit) instead of raw SQL.
Each returns an ActiveRecord::Relation you can chain until a terminal method (first, to_a, each).
find(id) looks up by primary key; first returns the first row by ordering.
Values in where are parameterized, so SQL injection is prevented for the common cases.
Don't call .all and load everything — constrain with where and limit.

sections.title: Spoken Answer
sections.content: ActiveRecord gives you chainable query methods instead of raw SQL. where of active true filters, order of created_at desc sorts, limit of ten caps the count, first returns the first row, find of id looks up by primary key, and all returns everything. Each method returns an ActiveRecord Relation — a lazy, chainable query — so you compose where, then order, then limit, and the SQL runs only when a terminal method like first, to_a, each, or count is called. This is the ActiveRecord Query Interface: composable, database-agnostic, and safe from SQL injection for the common cases because the values in where are parameterized. The common mistakes are calling all and loading the whole table, and using raw SQL with string interpolation where a query method is safer.

sections.title: Build the mental model
sections.content:
ActiveRecord gives you chainable query methods instead of raw SQL: Model.where(active: true), Model.order(created_at: :desc), Model.limit(10), Model.first, Model.find(id), Model.all.

Each returns an ActiveRecord relation you can chain (where(...).order(...).limit(...)) until you trigger it with a terminal method (first, to_a, each).

This is the ActiveRecord Query Interface — composable, database-agnostic, and safe from SQL injection for the common cases.

A common mistake is calling .all and loading everything, or using raw SQL with interpolation where a query method is safer.

sections.title: Chaining Query Methods
sections.content:
Each method returns a Relation you can chain; a terminal method runs the SQL.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  W[where] --> O[order] --> L[limit] --> F[first -> SQL runs]
```

sections.title: Basic querying
sections.content:
```ruby
# Chainable query methods (each returns a Relation):
User.where(active: true)                  # WHERE active = true
User.where(age: 18..30).order(name: :asc)   # filtered + sorted
User.limit(10)                              # limit 10

# Terminal methods run the SQL:
User.first                                 # first row
User.find(42)                              # by primary key
User.where(active: true).to_a              # load all into an array
User.count                                 # SELECT COUNT(*)

# Composition (no SQL until .first):
User.where(active: true).order(created_at: :desc).limit(5).first
```
